style_authority.note: Reads the surface as a 'calm utility character' operations tool and states 'Motion should remain subordinate to input'. Product context drives the verdict, though no explicit motion-policy authority check is shown.

reference_selection.note: Does not name any reference; interaction-physics content is applied (velocity handoff, clamped projection, bounded resistance), but the boundary formula is a generic overshoot/(1+|o|/64) rather than the canonical rubber-band model. No visible design-system or validation reference selection.

anti_generic_redesign.note: 'Should this animate?' approves only pointer attachment and a restrained settle and lists what not to tween. The section is short and less specific about which settle properties to drop.

evidence_level.note: Explicit 'Evidence level: L0 static'; findings marked 'not claims of observed runtime failure' and 'no frame cost was measured'. Timing values are labeled 'tuning hypothesis'.

verified_boundary.note: 'Verified here means source inspection only' with an unverified list that explicitly names animation precedence, focus behavior, and Reduced Motion output, plus 'moves above are proposed behavior, not completed fixes'.

design_moves.note: M1-M8 give concrete mechanics: pointer-ID capture, presentationYAtDown-based 1:1 tracking via a single transform owner, sample-before-cancel interruption, CSS px/s velocity handoff, gated projection, bounded resistance, and a JS + CSS Reduced Motion path. No hysteresis, and the boundary model is ad hoc.

scope_control.note: Most compact at 55 lines, with five findings, eight moves, and four tagged validation steps linked to findings. M8 (keyboard controls) is mildly outside motion scope.
